result.rationale: The formula is applied correctly (0.65 x 6.7 + 0.35 x 0.0 = 4.3) and I verified the news basis independently: NWS0022 and NWS0024 are genuinely benign capacity and appointment stories with no distress indicators, so a 0.0 news component is right. Healthy is defensible on the numbers, since closing the gap to the 35 threshold would require a payment score far above what even the 15-day peak supports. However, the payment input is a point-in-time 5 DPD reading taken near the favourable end of a volatile and self-described "deteriorating" series that peaked at 15 days late in June, so the score flatters the buyer on timing. Combined with a EUR 1.38M single invoice against a EUR 5.16M credit limit last reviewed in Oct 2024, this warrants monitoring despite the low band.

concerns.issue: The scored payment input (5 DPD) is a snapshot near the low end of a volatile range. The payment review records lateness rising from 3-9 days early in the year to a 15-day peak in June, with the most recent settlement at 6 days late, and labels the trend 'deteriorating'. Had the score been struck in June the payment component would have been materially worse; the Healthy band partly reflects observation timing rather than a stable improvement.

Concentration risk is not captured by the formula. A single open invoice of EUR 1.38M sits against a single insurer credit limit of EUR 5.16M, so one individual invoice absorbs a substantial share of the line. The score treats DPD alone and is indifferent to exposure size.

The credit line has not been reviewed since Oct 2024, which predates the entire late-payment pattern described in the review. The limit currently in force was set without sight of the deterioration now on record and should be re-underwritten.

Process note, immaterial to the outcome: the news component was driven by NWS0022 at 696 days old, the oldest of the four matched articles, when a more recent item (NWS0024, 104 days) was available. All four are severity 0 so the 0.0 result is unaffected, but the driver-selection logic appears not to prefer recency and could matter on a buyer with mixed-severity coverage.
